structured_output.question: On the Muon + lookahead tip (bs 1024, 6.5 epochs, ~49 steps/epoch, CIFAR-100), can the batch size be raised to 1536-2048 without losing accuracy per epoch? Fewer steps would cut the per-step Muon and lookahead overhead and give larger GEMMs (H1.2.3, untested). The search should find what the literature says about the critical batch size of orthogonalized and normalized-update optimizers (Muon, Shampoo/SOAP-like) compared with SGD. It should also cover how lr, momentum, weight decay and averaging horizon should be rescaled when the batch size grows at a fixed epoch budget in short, data-limited training. That evidence decides whether to run the batch-size experiment next and how to set the SGD-group lr/wd and the lookahead schedule for it.
queries: orthogonalized optimizer large batch scaling learning rate momentum
critical batch size Shampoo SOAP versus SGD Adam
batch size scaling weight averaging EMA horizon
learning rate scaling batch size fixed epoch budget short training
Muon hyperparameter transfer batch size weight decay
rubric: Reports how accuracy or loss at a fixed number of samples/epochs changes when the batch size varies, for Muon or another orthogonalized or preconditioned optimizer, ideally compared with SGD or Adam.
Gives concrete scaling rules for lr, momentum, weight decay or EMA/averaging horizon when batch size changes (e.g. sqrt or linear scaling, or the batch-size invariance of a normalized update).
Covers a short-horizon or data-limited regime (a few epochs, small image datasets or small models), or states explicitly whether its findings transfer to that regime.
Reports wall-clock or step-count tradeoffs, not just final accuracy after long training.
exclude: Methods that need pretrained weights, external data or distillation from a pretrained teacher (forbidden by RULES.md)
Test-time augmentation or anything that uses the test set (forbidden)
Multi-GPU or distributed data-parallel communication papers whose gains come from communication, not optimization
LLM-pretraining-only results at billions of tokens that have no transfer analysis
Re-testing ideas already refuted here: label smoothing 0.3, decaying lr to zero, BN recalibration, frequency-wise Muon, CUDA-graphing the Muon step
